## 上一轮交接 (task_context)

### 1. 🔴 硬约束 / 红线
- GPU 白名单 cuda:0/1/2/3 全部四张，均属本项目。无越界风险但须注意多实验抢占同一 GPU（grid_b_low_r3 就是因为没设 CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES 与 contamination_60_seed42_r2 撞 cuda:0 崩溃）
- 代码用 `AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained()`，是 continued pretraining 不是 from scratch。Experiments 节写了 "from random initialization" 是错的，已标 critical 但截至 handoff 未修复
- eval holdout 是纯人类数据（data/human/eval_holdout.jsonl, 67823 条 FineWeb），不是 "balanced real/synthetic"。Experiments 节描述也错了，同上已标 critical

### 2. 🖥️ 基础设施快照
- 服务器：westd-47453 (root)，代码根目录 /root/provenance_weight_training
- Python：/root/miniconda3/bin/python，conda activate base
- 模型：/root/provenance_weight_training/models/Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B（1.5GB pretrained, ModelScope 下载）
- 数据：data/scored_data.jsonl (ρ=0.4, 371K 条), data/scored_data_60.jsonl (ρ=0.6), data/human/eval_holdout.jsonl (67823 条)
- WANDB_MODE=disabled（大部分实验），无需查 W&B
- 本地 workspace：/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0509_10/projects/provenance_weight_training/

### 3. 📊 当前状态
**刚完成**：审查了 Introduction + Conclusion 写作、bs8_nmin2_seed42_r2 假失败（EXIT_CODE=129, 训练实际完成, eval PPL=17.73）、grid_b_low 三连失败、ess_only 三 seed 汇总、full_experiment_data.md 数据提取

**RUNNING 实验（截至 handoff）**：
- contamination_60_seed42_r2 — cuda:0, ρ=0.6 adaptive, ~10% 进度
- contamination_60_uniform_seed42 — cuda:1, ρ=0.6 uniform baseline, ~10% 进度  
- contamination_60_grid_b0_5_seed42 — cuda:3, ρ=0.6 grid b=0.5
- grid_b_low_seed42_r3 — cuda:0（已 failed，与 r2 撞 GPU）；grid_b_low_serial_seed42 QUEUED 等 GPU

**待 Director 决策**：grid_b_low 三连失败，建议拆成三条独立实验

### 4. 📋 待办（条件触发式）
- contamination_60_* 三个实验完成 → 审查 ρ=0.6 下 adaptive vs uniform vs grid 对比，验证 "graceful degradation" claim
- grid_b_low_serial_seed42 启动/完成 → 验证 b=0.1/0.2/0.3 的 PPL 是否接近 uniform，确认 b=0.5 是 lower useful bound
- Results / Discussion / Abstract 写作 worker 完成 → 章节对抗审查（重点：PPL 数字与 table1_data.md 一致性、88.6% claim 是否修正、"from random init" 是否修正）
- bs8_nmin2_seed42_r2 eval 已出 PPL=17.73 → 如果 Agent 用这个数字写 batch size robustness 结论，注意 bs8 的 PPL(17.73) 比 bs4(17.65) 差很多，可能因为 n_min=2 在 bs=8 下约束力不同

### 5. 🎯 战略上下文
**核心结论**：adaptive b* (τ=0.8, n_min=2) 3-seed mean PPL=17.651，vs grid-best(b=0.5)=17.646，vs uniform=17.693。Adaptive 恢复 grid-best 89.4% 的改善（ratio-of-means），无需 grid search。ESS-only(17.72) 劣于 uniform，证明 min-intervention > max-intervention。

**已提交未修复的 critical/warning 汇总**：
1. [critical] Experiments "from random initialization" → 应为 "continued pretraining"
2. [critical] Experiments "balanced real/synthetic test set" → eval 是纯人类数据
3. [critical] Introduction vs Experiments 对同一事实矛盾（continued vs random init）
4. [warning] Conclusion PPL "17.651 vs 17.646" 需报告 mean±std
5. [warning] "calibration > discrimination" claim 无直接实验支撑
6. [warning] Method 节 line 136 "46.7% hitting ceiling at b_max=20" 数据错误（46.7% 是 b*≥2 不是 b*=b_max）
7. [warning] Related Work cheng_2025 "20-60%" 来源需核实

**易错点**：
- table1_data.md 里 uniform seed42 PPL=17.690，但 unified_nmin_eval 里的 baseline 是 17.6939。前者是 3 位小数截断，注意对比时用哪个源
- adaptive_seed42 (n_min=3, legacy) vs adaptive_fix_seed42 (n_min=2, correct) — 论文用的是 fix 版本，但 registry 里两个都在，别搞混
- bs8 实验 PPL=17.73 比 bs4 差很多，如果 Agent 试图 claim "batch size robust"，这个数据不支持

## agent-ml-research
ML research experiment management tools

attachment.content:
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

file.content:
\paragraph{Training Data.}
We sample a 132M-token subset of FineWeb~\citep{penedo2024fineweb} as the real-data source.
To simulate web-scale synthetic contamination, we generate continuations with Qwen3-0.6B~\citep{yang2025qwen3}---the same model we continue pretraining---and inject them at ratio $\rho = 0.4$ via uniform random mixing.
This self-contamination design---where the model's own outputs are mixed back into its training data---creates a particularly challenging detection scenario, as generator and trainee share identical pretrained weights.

\paragraph{Detector.}
We train a TF-IDF + Logistic Regression classifier on a held-out labeled split, achieving AUC\,=\,0.939 with calibrated ECE\,=\,0.048 after temperature scaling ($T = 0.204$).
The resulting $q$-scores have mean 0.60, standard deviation 0.37, and median 0.71, with 46.3\% of samples in the uncertain range $[0.2, 0.8]$.
We use this lightweight detector rather than neural alternatives (e.g., ModernBERT at AUC\,${\geq}$\,0.98 in \citealt{drayson2025detection}) to test whether score \emph{calibration} may matter as much as raw discrimination for reweighting.

\paragraph{Training.}
We continue pretraining Qwen3-0.6B for 6{,}103 steps (batch size 4, gradient accumulation 4, effective batch 16) with AdamW, cosine schedule (peak lr\,=\,$5{\times}10^{-5}$), max sequence length 2048, and bf16 precision.
The pretrained checkpoint starts at PPL\,=\,22.97 on our held-out set; after continued pretraining, the best method (adaptive $\bstar$) reaches $17.651 {\pm} 0.007$ across three seeds ($\Delta$PPL\,=\,$-5.319$, $-23.2\%$).
All main comparisons use three random seeds (42, 123, 456).
We note that method-level differences (${\sim}0.04$ PPL between adaptive and uniform) are small in absolute terms but arise in a regime where the model is already well-optimized; the $5{+}$ PPL drop from pretraining absorbs the easy gains, making further improvement from data curation increasingly difficult.

\paragraph{Evaluation.}
We report held-out perplexity (PPL) on a balanced real/synthetic test set via sliding-window evaluation (stride 1024, 4.08M tokens).
All evaluations are post-hoc with a unified pipeline; training involves no inline evaluation.

\paragraph{Methods.}
We compare five approaches:
\begin{itemize}[nosep,leftmargin=*]
  \item \textbf{Uniform}: $w_j = 1$ for all $j$ (no contamination handling).
  \item \textbf{Grid-$b$}: fixed $b \in \{0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 3.0, 5.0\}$, best selected post-hoc by held-out PPL.
        Represents validation-based selection~\citep{drayson2025detection}.
  \item \textbf{ESS-only}: $b^* = \max\{b : \mathrm{ESS}(b) \geq n_{\min}\}$, the maximum-intervention variant retaining only the stability constraint, ablating $\alpha_{\mathrm{eff}}$.
  \item \textbf{Golden Ratio}: $w = 1/\varphi \approx 0.618$ for synthetic ($q_j > 0.5$), $w = 1$ otherwise~\citep{he2025golden}.
        Requires known provenance labels (oracle).
  \item \textbf{Adaptive} (ours): per-batch $b^*$ from the dual-constraint formulation (\S\ref{sec:method}), with $\tau = 0.8$ and $n_{\min} = 2$ (half the micro-batch size).

1	\section{Results}
2	\label{sec:results}
3	
4	\subsection{Main Comparison}
5	
6	Table~\ref{tab:main} reports held-out perplexity across methods and seeds.
7	Adaptive reweighting achieves mean PPL 17.651, matching grid-best ($b{=}0.5$, mean 17.646) within seed-to-seed variance: the per-seed gap never exceeds 0.007, less than half the cross-seed range of the uniform baseline (17.686--17.702).
8	This parity comes at zero validation cost---grid search requires $|\mathcal{B}|$ complete training runs (six in our sweep), whereas adaptive requires one.
9	
10	The grid-$b$ sweep reveals monotonically increasing PPL from $b{=}0.5$ to $b{=}5.0$ (17.651 to 17.738 on seed 42; full sweep in Appendix~\ref{app:grid}), confirming that exponent selection is consequential.
11	The optimal $b{=}0.5$ differs from the $b{=}10$ reported by \citet{drayson_2025_detection_collapse} at comparable model scale, underscoring the model-dependence of fixed-exponent selection.
12	
13	ESS-only (maximum intervention) yields PPL 17.728 on seed 42, \emph{worse} than uniform (17.694) by 0.034.
14	Removing $\alpha_{\mathrm{eff}}$ and maximizing $b$ subject only to $\mathrm{ESS} \geq n_{\min}$ leads to over-downweighting that degrades training, providing direct evidence for the minimum-intervention principle.
15	
16	The Golden Ratio oracle~\citep{he_2025_golden_ratio} achieves PPL 17.654 on seed 42 using known provenance labels.
17	Adaptive reaches within 0.001 of this upper bound without provenance access, suggesting the dual constraint recovers near-optimal weights from noisy detector scores alone.
18	
19	The adaptive $b^*$ distribution (median 0.87, IQR $[0.54, 1.51]$, mean 1.40) confirms that most batches need only moderate intervention.
20	The constraint regime breakdown in \S\ref{sec:algorithm} shows that $\alpha_{\mathrm{eff}}$ prevents over-intervention in the 40\% of reweighted batches where moderate $b$ already meets the quality target.
21	
22	\begin{table}[t]
23	\centering
24	\small
25	\begin{tabular}{@{}lcccc@{}}
26	\toprule
27	\textbf{Method} & \textbf{Seed 42} & \textbf{Seed 123} & \textbf{Seed 456} & \textbf{Mean} \\
28	\midrule
29	Uniform               & 17.694 & 17.686 & 17.702 & 17.694 \\
30	Grid-best ($b{=}0.5$) & \textbf{17.651} & \textbf{17.638} & \textbf{17.650} & \textbf{17.646} \\
31	ESS-only$^\dagger$     & 17.728 & --     & --     & --     \\
32	Golden Ratio$^\dagger$ & 17.654 & --     & --     & --     \\
33	\midrule
34	Adaptive (ours)        & 17.653 & 17.643 & 17.657 & 17.651 \\
35	\bottomrule
36	\end{tabular}
37	\caption{Held-out perplexity (PPL, $\downarrow$).
38	Grid-best selects the optimal fixed $b$ post-hoc from six candidates.
39	$^\dagger$Evaluated on seed 42 only; remaining seeds in progress.
40	Best per column in \textbf{bold}.}
41	\label{tab:main}
42	\end{table}
43	
44	\subsection{Sensitivity Analysis}
45	
46	\paragraph{Quality threshold $\tau$.}
47	Table~\ref{tab:tau} varies $\tau$ while holding $n_{\min} = 2$ (seed 42).
48	All values in $\tau \in [0.5, 0.8]$ improve over uniform, with $\tau = 0.8$ achieving the lowest PPL (17.653).
49	Higher $\tau$ demands greater $\alpha_{\mathrm{eff}}$, forcing the solver to increase $b^*$: mean $\bar{b}^*$ rises monotonically from 0.39 at $\tau{=}0.5$ to 3.08 at $\tau{=}0.95$.
50	Below 0.8, reweighting is too gentle to fully exploit the detector signal; above, $b^*$ inflates past diminishing returns and PPL degrades.
51	The range $[0.5, 0.8]$ provides a wide safe operating region, with $\tau = 0.8$ as the recommended default.
52	
53	\begin{table}[t]
54	\centering
55	\small
56	\begin{tabular}{@{}cccc@{}}
57	\toprule
58	$\tau$ & \textbf{PPL} & $\Delta_{\mathrm{unif}}$ & $\bar{b}^*$ \\
59	\midrule
60	0.50 & 17.688 & $-$0.006 & 0.39 \\
61	0.60 & 17.681 & $-$0.013 & 0.59 \\
62	0.70 & 17.679 & $-$0.015 & 0.89 \\
63	\textbf{0.80} & \textbf{17.653} & $\mathbf{-0.041}$ & \textbf{1.40} \\
64	0.90 & 17.712 & $+$0.018 & 2.36 \\
65	0.95 & 17.723 & $+$0.029 & 3.08 \\
66	\bottomrule
67	\end{tabular}
68	\caption{Sensitivity to $\tau$ (seed 42, $n_{\min}{=}2$, $\rho{=}0.4$).
69	$\Delta_{\mathrm{unif}}$: PPL change vs.\ uniform baseline (17.694).
70	$\bar{b}^*$: mean adaptive exponent across batches.}
71	\label{tab:tau}
72	\end{table}
73

\section{Results}
\label{sec:results}

\subsection{Main Comparison}

Table~\ref{tab:main} reports held-out perplexity across methods and seeds.
Adaptive reweighting achieves mean PPL 17.651, matching grid-best ($b{=}0.5$, mean 17.646) within seed-to-seed variance: the per-seed gap never exceeds 0.007, less than half the cross-seed range of the uniform baseline (17.686--17.702).
This parity comes at zero validation cost---grid search requires $|\mathcal{B}|$ complete training runs (six in our sweep), whereas adaptive requires one.

The grid-$b$ sweep reveals monotonically increasing PPL from $b{=}0.5$ to $b{=}5.0$ (17.651 to 17.738 on seed 42; full sweep in Appendix~\ref{app:grid}), confirming that exponent selection is consequential.
The optimal $b{=}0.5$ differs from the $b{=}10$ reported by \citet{drayson_2025_detection_collapse} at comparable model scale, underscoring the model-dependence of fixed-exponent selection.

ESS-only (maximum intervention) yields PPL 17.728 on seed 42, \emph{worse} than uniform (17.694) by 0.034.
Removing $\alpha_{\mathrm{eff}}$ and maximizing $b$ subject only to $\mathrm{ESS} \geq n_{\min}$ leads to over-downweighting that degrades training, providing direct evidence for the minimum-intervention principle.

The Golden Ratio oracle~\citep{he_2025_golden_ratio} achieves PPL 17.654 on seed 42 using known provenance labels.
Adaptive reaches within 0.001 of this upper bound without provenance access, suggesting the dual constraint recovers near-optimal weights from noisy detector scores alone.

The adaptive $b^*$ distribution (median 0.87, IQR $[0.54, 1.51]$, mean 1.40) confirms that most batches need only moderate intervention.
The constraint regime breakdown in \S\ref{sec:algorithm} shows that $\alpha_{\mathrm{eff}}$ prevents over-intervention in the 40\% of reweighted batches where moderate $b$ already meets the quality target.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}lcccc@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Method} & \textbf{Seed 42} & \textbf{Seed 123} & \textbf{Seed 456} & \textbf{Mean} \\
\midrule
Uniform               & 17.694 & 17.686 & 17.702 & 17.694 \\
Grid-best ($b{=}0.5$) & \textbf{17.651} & \textbf{17.638} & \textbf{17.650} & \textbf{17.646} \\
ESS-only$^\dagger$     & 17.728 & --     & --     & --     \\
Golden Ratio$^\dagger$ & 17.654 & --     & --     & --     \\
\midrule
Adaptive (ours)        & 17.653 & 17.643 & 17.657 & 17.651 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\caption{Held-out perplexity (PPL, $\downarrow$).
Grid-best selects the optimal fixed $b$ post-hoc from six candidates.
$^\dagger$Evaluated on seed 42 only; remaining seeds in progress.
Best per column in \textbf{bold}.}
\label{tab:main}
\end{table}

\subsection{Sensitivity Analysis}

\paragraph{Quality threshold $\tau$.}
Table~\ref{tab:tau} varies $\tau$ while holding $n_{\min} = 2$ (seed 42).
All values in $\tau \in [0.5, 0.8]$ improve over uniform, with $\tau = 0.8$ achieving the lowest PPL (17.653).
Higher $\tau$ demands greater $\alpha_{\mathrm{eff}}$, forcing the solver to increase $b^*$: mean $\bar{b}^*$ rises monotonically from 0.39 at $\tau{=}0.5$ to 3.08 at $\tau{=}0.95$.
Below 0.8, reweighting is too gentle to fully exploit the detector signal; above, $b^*$ inflates past diminishing returns and PPL degrades.
The range $[0.5, 0.8]$ provides a wide safe operating region, with $\tau = 0.8$ as the recommended default.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}cccc@{}}
\toprule
$\tau$ & \textbf{PPL} & $\Delta_{\mathrm{unif}}$ & $\bar{b}^*$ \\
\midrule
0.50 & 17.688 & $-$0.006 & 0.39 \\
0.60 & 17.681 & $-$0.013 & 0.59 \\
0.70 & 17.679 & $-$0.015 & 0.89 \\
\textbf{0.80} & \textbf{17.653} & $\mathbf{-0.041}$ & \textbf{1.40} \\
0.90 & 17.712 & $+$0.018 & 2.36 \\
0.95 & 17.723 & $+$0.029 & 3.08 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\caption{Sensitivity to $\tau$ (seed 42, $n_{\min}{=}2$, $\rho{=}0.4$).
$\Delta_{\mathrm{unif}}$: PPL change vs.\ uniform baseline (17.694).
$\bar{b}^*$: mean adaptive exponent across batches.}
\label{tab:tau}
\end{table}

\paragraph{Minimum ESS $n_{\min}$.}
Removing the ESS floor ($n_{\min} = 1$) allows $b^*$ to inflate to mean 7.20, degrading PPL to 17.789---0.095 worse than uniform.
At $n_{\min} = 2$ ($= \lfloor B/2 \rfloor$ for batch size $B{=}4$), PPL stabilizes at 17.653; $n_{\min} = 3$ yields a comparable 17.651.
The coupling $n_{\min} = \lfloor B/2 \rfloor$ provides a configuration-aware default that balances reweighting headroom against gradient stability.
